rows.derivation: START-NULL: nothing raised -> null arm. DECL-SAME: RAISE E (14.9.29.4 GR2) -> inside USE AFTER EO the register IS E (identity relation). AFTER-SAME: declarative completes normally, current exception unchanged. NAMED-NULL: RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-NAMED sets EXCEPTION-OBJECT to null (14.9.29.4 GR1) -> null arm after a named raise. Lines START-NULL/DECL-SAME/AFTER-SAME/NAMED-NULL pin GR1.
rows.notes: Also passes at --std 2023. Subprogram passes E BY CONTENT because 14.9.4.3 SR10 forbids BY REFERENCE for class-object items (compiler COBOLNET1679 correctly refused my first draft).

rows.derivation: SUB-SAME: separately compiled program L1C08B (same run unit) reads EXCEPTION-OBJECT after main's RAISE E and finds it identical to main's E (passed as a parameter); per-program registers would give SUB-NULL. SUB-NULL: after main's named raise, B sees the null main left -> one shared register both ways.
rows.notes: Shares the program with GR1; lines SUB-SAME and SUB-NULL pin GR2.

Needs a non-COBOL activating element (a .NET host calling ProgramRegistry.CallProgram). The conformance runner only compiles and runs COBOL sources, so it cannot drive this. A unit/integration test with a C# host would be the right witness.

rows.derivation: C directly contains D (ended by END PROGRAM L1C08D) and then E; F follows END PROGRAM L1C08C. Each has its own X. D X=DDDD: D's own X. E X=EEEE: END PROGRAM L1C08D ended D, so E is directly contained in C, and C may CALL it (8.4.6.3 1)). F X=FFFF: END PROGRAM L1C08C ended C, so F is a separate program. C X=OUTER: C's X is untouched.
rows.notes: Program units only (1985+). OO/function end markers are not covered by this golden.

rows.derivation: `05 A OF G PIC X(3).` (qualified) and `05 A(1) PIC X(3).` (subscripted) each break SR1. Everything else in the programs is valid, so both must be rejected at 85/2002/2014/2023.
rows.notes: The rejection is the generic parse error COBOL0001, which is acceptable because this is a pure syntax rule (the grammar's declaration slot takes a single word). The .err files use the specific message heads: COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near 'OF' and COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near '('. Rejected at all four editions.

rows.derivation: Four programs cover the four legal shapes. G-START/G-END: the header alone. H ED=12,50: CONFIGURATION only, and its DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA takes effect. I REC=IREC: INPUT-OUTPUT only, and the SELECTed file is written and read back. J ED=03,25 REC=JREC: both sections in format order, both in effect. Negative: INPUT-OUTPUT placed before CONFIGURATION breaks the fixed order of the format, so it must be rejected.
rows.notes: The negative is rejected at 85/2002/2014/2023 with COBOL0001: unexpected 'CONFIGURATION'. A generic parse code is acceptable because this is a general-format rule.

rows.derivation: FLOAT-BINARY-64 items hold NaN/+inf (SET CONTENT). Checking is ON, and the USE declarative prints EXCEPTION-STATUS and does RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT. These raise nothing: the class conditions (FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER, FLOAT-INFINITY), the sign condition (POSITIVE), and MOVE to FLOAT-BINARY-64 HIGH-ORDER-LEFT and HIGH-ORDER-RIGHT (same usage, endianness excepted). Each of these gives one CAUGHT=EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE: MOVE to FLOAT-BINARY-32 (different standard usage), MOVE to S9(5), the relation IF FI > 0 (resume after END-IF, so no REL-TRUE), and COMPUTE N = FN + 1.
rows.notes: Also passes at 2023. The VALIDATE exemption is not exercised because VALIDATE is not claimed (A.4.14). FLOAT-DECIMAL is refused by documented choice. The class-condition exemption quote is shared verbatim with rule 1), so cite.py resolves that fragment to 3)'s sibling; the golden cites the full rule-3 sentence.

rows.derivation: BEFORE; DECL-START (USE AFTER EC-USER-STOPIT runs); M-START (directly activated element); N-STOPS (indirectly activated element executes STOP RUN, 14.9.42.4 6)). Under rule 2) the declarative does not complete normally, so M-END, DECL-END and AFTER-RAISE never appear.
rows.notes: Exercises the 'indirectly' arm (the chain declarative -> M -> N). Also passes at 2023.

rows.derivation: EC-OVERFLOW-STRING (NF) is enabled; there is no ON OVERFLOW, WHEN or USE. STRING rules apply: 8) a) stops the transfer, giving T=ABCD P=05, and 8) e) ignores NOT ON OVERFLOW, so no NOT-OVF. ST=EC-OVERFLOW-STRING shows the condition was raised (enabled branch). EC-USER-GOON is enabled with no handler, so RAISE acts as CONTINUE: AFTER-RAISE, then ST=EC-USER-GOON.
